places.ds: The Church of St Louis (French: Église Saint-Louis) is a historic Roman Catholic church in the 15th arrondissement of Marseille, France. It was designed in the Bauhaus architectural style by Jean-Louis Sourdeau, with additional sculptures designed by Carlo Sarrabezolles. Its construction was completed in 1935.

The CMA CGM Tower is a 147-metre (482 ft) tall skyscraper in Euroméditerranée, the central business district of Marseille, France. Designed by Zaha Hadid, it is the headquarters for CMA CGM, one of the world's major freight companies, hosting 2,200 employees in the office previously spread over seven sites. Zaha Hadid was selected to design the building in November 2004, and it became her first tower.

The Phare de Sainte-Marie is an inactive lighthouse built to mark the harbor of Marseille, France. Completed in 1855, it is made of natural-finished local limestone and stands 70 feet high. It is located at the north side of the Passe de la Joliette.

Marseille Cathedral (French: Cathédrale Notre-Dame-de-la-Major or Cathédrale de La Major or simply La Major; Occitan: Catedrala Nòstra Dòna de la Major) is a Roman Catholic cathedral and a national monument of France. Located in Marseille, it has been a basilica minor since 1896. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Marseille (the Diocese of Marseille until its elevation in 1948).

The Musée Regards de Provence (French: [myze ʁəɡaʁ d(ə) pʁɔvɑ̃s]) is an art museum in Marseille, France. It was opened in 2013 by the Fondation Regards de Provence in the former Station sanitaire du Port de Marseille in the 2nd arrondissement amid the Marseille-Provence 2013 celebrations. It has a collection of over 850 art pieces related to Southern France, the Mediterranean coast and Provence.

The Porte d'Aix (French pronunciation: [pɔʁt dɛks]; lit. 'Gate of Aix'; Occitan: Pòrt d'Ais), formerly known as the Porte Royale (Pòrt Reial), is a triumphal arch in Marseille, southern France, marking the old entry point to the city on the road from Aix-en-Provence. The classical design by Michel-Robert Penchaud was inspired by the triumphal arches of the Roman Empire.

The Palais du Pharo (French pronunciation: [palɛ dy faʁo] Occitan: Palais del Pharo) is a palace in Marseille, southern France, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, west of the Old Port (Vieux-Port). It was built in Second Empire style by Emperor Napoleon III for Empress Eugénie, starting in 1858. However, at the fall of the Second Empire in 1870, the building had just been finished.

places.ds: The Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations (Mucem or MuCEM; French: Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée; Occitan: Museu de las Civilizacions Europèas e Mediterranèas) is an ethnology national museum in Marseille, France.

places.ds: The Marseille transporter bridge, inaugurated in 1905 and destroyed in 1944, was a crossing of the Old Port of Marseille, designed by engineer Ferdinand Arnodin.
The Église Saint-Cannat is a Roman Catholic church in Marseille.

The Hôtel de Ville (French pronunciation: [otɛl də vil], City Hall; Occitan: Ostal de Vila) is a historic building in Marseille, Bouches-du-Rhône, southern France, standing on Quai du Port. It was designated a monument historique by the French government in 1948.
The Hôtel Pesciolini is a hôtel particulier in the 1st arrondissement of Marseille, France. It has been listed as an official historical monument since March 8, 1929.
The Marseille History Museum (French: Musée d'Histoire de Marseille; Occitan: Museu d'Istòria de Marselha) is the local historical and archaeological museum of Marseille in France.

about.ds: Marseille (Occitan: Marselha) is a city in southern France, the prefecture of the Bouches-du-Rhône department and of the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. Situated in Provence, it marks the eastern end of the Côte Bleue on the Mediterranean coast. Marseille is the second-most populous city proper in France, after Paris, with 886,040 inhabitants in 2023 over a municipal territory of 241 km2 (93 sq mi).
